sentences.text:

The present criminal revision has been filed against the impugned judgment and order dated 10.01.2024 passed by the Additional District Judge / Special Judge (POCSO Act), Children's Court Ghazipur in Juvenile Criminal Appeal No. 60 of 2021 and order dated 12.08.2021 passed by the Juvenile Justice Board, Ghazipur whereby the trial court has referred the matter for adult trial of revisionist as adult in Case Crime No. 160 of 2019, under Sections- 376 IPC and Section of POCSO Act.

entities.text: Additional District Judge / Special Judge (POCSO Act), Children's Court Ghazipur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
-
The Juvenile Justice Board, Ghazipur, by its order dated 17.01.2020, declared the revisionist to be a Juvenile and, upon finding his age to be above 16 years, directed his preliminary assessment under Section 15 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Pursuant thereto, a report was obtained from a psychologist, wherein his mental capacity was assessed at 55, i.e., below average.

In other respects, however, he was found to be fit and capable of understanding the consequences of his acts, and accordingly, he was directed to be tried as an adult in terms of Section 18(3) of the Act.

The aforesaid order was thereafter challenged before the Children's Court /
Appellate Court.

-
The Appellate Court has earlier decided the issue against the revisionist by the order dated 20.09.2021 which was subjected to challenge before this court vide Criminal Revision No. 3000 of 2021 and after setting aside the earlier order dated 20.09.2021 this court directed the Appellate Court to decide the issue again.

The Appellate Court has considered the issue again and has found X- Juvenile vs State Of Up And 3 Others on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103124208/
2

entities.text: X- Juvenile vs State Of Up And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: that although
the intelligence of Juvenile was below average but he has committed forceful rape of 11-12 years old girl.
In his examination by the Juvenile Justice Board, Ghazipur, his behaviour was found to be normal.
He was physically and mentally found to be healthy and capable of understanding the consequences of his act.
Hence, the Appellate Court has again decided the issue against the revisionist.

-
This court does not finds any illegality in the findings recorded by the Appellate Court.

Merely on the ground that the intelligence of revisionist was below average, it cannot be said that he was not physically and mentally capable of committing the alleged offence nor it can be said that he was not aware of the consequences of the act done by him.
It is a case of forceful rape of a minor girl and there is no element of consent in law involved.

-
The Apex Court in the case of Parag Bhati (Juvenile) through Legal Guardian ? Mother- Smt. Rajni Bhati vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Another, 2016 0 Supreme(SC) 366, has held that the benevolent provisions of Juvenile Justice Act, cannot be allowed to be misused where heinous crime is committed by an accused in paragraph nos. 26 and 27 are as follows :-

entities.text: Rajni Bhati vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Another, 2016 0 Supreme(SC) 366
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "(26) It is no doubt true that if there is a clear and unambiguous case in favour of the juvenile accused that he was a minor below the age of 18 years on the date of the incident and the documentary evidence at least prima facie proves the same, he would be entitled to the special protection under the JJ Act.

But when an accused commits a grave and heinous offence and thereafter attempts to take statutory shelter under the guise of being a minor, a casual or cavalier approach while recording as to whether an accused is a juvenile or not cannot be permitted as the courts are enjoined upon to perform their duties with the object of protecting the confidence of common man in the institution entrusted with the administration of justice.

(27) The benefit of the principle of benevolent legislation attached to the JJ Act would thus apply to only such cases wherein the accused is held to be a juvenile on the basis of at least prima facie evidence regarding his minority as the benefit of the possibilities of two views in regard to the age of the alleged accused who is involved in grave and serious offence which he committed and gave effect to it in a well-planned manner reflecting his maturity of mind rather than innocence indicating that his plea of juvenility is more in the nature of a shield to dodge or dupe the arms of law, cannot be allowed to come to his rescue."

-
In view of the aforesaid consideration, the order passed by the Revisional Court is hereby affirmed.

Accordingly, the criminal revision stands dismissed.
